Select a rule on the left
Match only when the exact case is used
Uppercase and lowercase letters must match exactly. With the word "Spam", the rule won\'t trigger on "spam" or "SPAM".
Ignore partial matches inside longer words
The rule won\'t fire if the word is just part of another word. A hyphen now counts as part of a word too, so "some-thing" no longer matches a rule for "thing".
Advanced: treat the pattern as a regex
The pattern is read as a regular expression instead of plain text. For example, "time.?out" catches both "timeout" and "time-out".
Skip text inside links and clip URLs
Links and clip URLs are skipped entirely when the rule checks for matches. Prevents accidental hits — e.g. a clip link ending in "-Z" no longer triggers a rule for "Z".
